en: Śivabhujaṅgamam (The Serpent of Śiva)
With temples dripping ichor where swarms of bees gather,
with a moving and beautiful trunk, and skilled in protecting the world;
with gleaming tusks, he is fierce in shattering calamities.
I worship Vakratuṇḍa, who is a mass of love for Śiva. || 1 ||
Without beginning or end, the primordial, supreme reality, whose nature is consciousness, the one, the fourth state (turīya), immeasurable,
sought after by Hari and Brahmā, and whose form is the Supreme Brahman— You.
I praise the great splendor of Śiva, which transcends both mind and speech. || 2 ||
Seated upon a lion-throne extending from his own power (Sva-śakti) to the power of others (Para-śakti), adorned on all his limbs with beautiful ornaments of precious gems,
and wearing a crown of matted hair, the lord of serpents, the moon, the Ganges, bones, and a skull;
We praise the five-faced one, whose friend is the Supreme Power. || 3 ||

Who indeed can know You—the Supreme, beyond the thirty-six principles and the incomparable knowledge (vidyā)—by means of the five faces beginning with Śiva, Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, and Vāma, or by the six limbs? 4.
This form of Śiva within is sewn together with a thread of qualities: one half is as red as the luster of a stream of coral, while the other half is dark with the majestic splendor of sapphires.
I remember the cause for both the attainment of Smara and his downfall. || 5 ||
I bow to your lotus feet, O Śambhu, which are adorned by the mandāra garlands from the crowns of the lords of gods and asuras who have come to serve you;
which are a boat for the ocean of worldly existence, and which are to be meditated upon by Bhavānī.
O Jagannātha, my protector, Lord of Gaurī, compassionate toward those who have sought refuge, remover of the distress of the afflicted,
embodiment of a multitude of splendors, sole kinsman of all!
Salutations to you, salutations to you; may there be salutations to you again and again. || 7 ||
O Virūpākṣa, Lord of the Universe, Primordial God of the Universe, O Śambhu, root of the three Vedas, O Śiva, O Tryambaka—you are he!
Be gracious; remember us and protect us for the sake of liberation.
O Three-eyed One, attain forgiveness; protect me with joy! || 8 ||
Addressing you as "Mahādeva, Lord of Gods, God of Gods, Foe of Smara, Destroyer of Cities, Foe of Yama,
Hara," I shall remember you with devotion.
Therefore, O compassionate Lord, be gracious to me. || 9 ||
"There is no other refuge for one who has sought protection but You;

be gracious, and let Your mere remembrance destroy my wretchedness. If this were not so, O Compassionate One, it would mean a loss of Your affection for Your devotees; therefore, remain ever present with me."
This is the time for giving; I am the recipient of the gift, and you alone are the giver. I beg of no one other than you: grant me steadfast devotion to you.
O compassionate Śambhu, I have attained my purpose because of that. || 11 ||
If you know me to be a beast, mount that very one; or if you call me "defiled," place that very one upon your head.
Furthermore, even that double-tongued serpent shall be your neck-ornament.
O Śarva, all those who have been accepted by you are indeed blessed. || 12 ||
I am unable to commit even the slightest act of malice toward another;
O Lord of the Mountain, I do not understand how you can be pleased with me, for you are likewise pleased with anyone who harms his wife and children or betrays his father. 13.
Even while worshipping You, the Great Lord, he was unable to perform the praise, meditation, and worship according to the prescribed rules;
yet, to protect his son who was trembling before him, Mṛkaṇḍu took refuge in Your lotus feet, which extinguish even the life-force of Yama.

O Śambhu, you are the primordial physician and the medicine— your ash— for those afflicted by diseases of the head, eyes, and heart, by piercing pain, urinary disorders, fever, hemorrhoids, consumption, hiccup, and poison;
for the sake of lightness of body, restore us to health.
"I am poor, I am wretched, I am broken, I suffer, I am despondent, I am exhausted, and I am weary;
O Śambhu, you are the inner self of all living beings."
O Lord, you do not know my intent; protect me! || 16 ||
O Three-eyed One, wherever your sidelong glance falls for even a moment, both the Earth and Lakṣmī herself choose that man,
adorned with crowns, shimmering chowries, umbrellas, garlands, girdles, elephants, silken garments, and various exquisite ornaments.
To Bhavānī and also to Bhava, to the Mother and to the Father, to Mṛḍānī and also to Mṛḍa, to Aghahnyā and to Makhaghna,
to Śivāṅgī and to Śivāṅga, we offer [homage] to Śivā.
Salutation to Śiva, to Ambikā, and to Tryambaka. || 18 ||
O Lord, perceiving my own insignificance and your greatness, protect me with your compassionate gaze;
I am incapable of praising the majesty of your auspicious self.
Forgive the offense I have committed according to my own power. || 19 ||
When the clanging sound of the bells on the necks of Time’s enemies reaches your ear-canal,
my child, mount the Lord of Bulls, the divine vehicle, and comfort Him by saying, "Do not fear."
When the messengers of Kṛtānta appear before me with harsh speech and terrifying forms,
then may my mind abide in Your lotus feet.
How may it become motionless? Salutations to you, O Śambhu! || 21 ||
When I lie down, writhing in unbearable agony, sighing and uttering indistinct cries,
then [let there be] your [vision of] that [place] adorned by the waters of Jahnu’s daughter.
May the circle of matted locks be the temple of my mind. || 22 ||
When his sons, friends, and others weep in my presence, crying, "Alas! What kind of state is this for him?",
then, O Lord of the gods, O Lord of Gaurī, O Śambhu!
"Salutations to Śiva," I shall speak this incessantly. || 23 ||
When those who behold me might speak such words as, "This one does not know us; he is merely a dog's breath," then,
O Destroyer of Tripura, I shall clearly meditate upon you, adorned with ashes and entwined by serpents.
When there is no longer great delusion within my own body regarding the doubt of a body for torment, then, O Lord,
[I shall behold You] who resembles the moon in the sky.
O Enemy of Smara, salutation to your body; O Smara, salutation to you. || 25 ||

O Mahādeva, when I shall go upon that path which is beyond darkness, without a resting place, and devoid of water or people, then, blocking the path of Death (Kṛtānta), grant me that which is pleasing to my mind.
O Mahādeva, when I remember Raurava and the other hells and, out of fear, fall into a terrible delusion, then alas,
O Lord whose crest is the crescent moon, who will deliver me— helpless and dependent on another? (27)

When fear arises from Death, whose power is as insurmountable as a white-winged palm tree, then protect me, O Beloved of Pārvatī, out of your disposition of affection for your devotees; there is no other.
I do not see anyone who could destroy such as I am. || 28 ||
"Right now, right now, death will come to me"—alas, I am constantly tormented by such thoughts!
How indeed may this fear of death not arise? Salutations to you, O Blue-throated One, the goal of all goals! (29)
Beholding Kṛtānta (Death) carrying away all without restraint, from the young to the old, I have become terrified;
O Lord of Bhavānī, by the divine grace of Your lotus feet at the time of death, may I become fearless.
O Lord of the World, O God, may I abandon the unbearable sufferings of old age, birth, dwelling in the womb, and so forth;
for me there is no other refuge but you, O Śambhu, O Compassionate One—to whom else do your mercies not awaken? (31)
The word "Śivāya," preceded by "namaḥ," which expresses the ultimate reality, brings about liberation and destroys death for one who remembers it;
O Maheśāna, do not depart from my mind or my speech.
Always grant me this gift. || 32 ||
O Mother, beloved of the moon-crested Lord, look upon me too; you are the medicine for the pacification of the disease of worldly existence.
O boat of your lotus feet, carry me today to the further shore of this ocean of saṃsāra, in which I am submerged and burdened by manifold afflictions.

May those deities be sufficient for our protection— those who possess flames sprouting from brows and eyes that do not blink, who shine with the beauty of lovely, trembling thighs that are not left-side (but right), whose ornaments are special serpents wandering about without a body, and who are not adorned with a crescent moon upon their crests.

I do not acknowledge any other god than the Lord who is without a throat, yet possesses the Kaṇṭhaka horse; who is without limbs, yet has the serpent as his arm; who is without hands, yet holds a skull; who is without a forehead, yet has the crescent moon; and who is without a wife, yet has Pārvatī as his consort. I do not acknowledge any other; I do not acknowledge any other.
O Mahādeva, O Śambhu, O Lord of the Mountain, O wielder of the trident, since everything shines as yours, I recognize no deity other than Śiva;
I am Śiva, I am Śiva, I am Śiva, I am Śiva. (36)
From whom this manifold world was born,
in whom it finds its stability, and into whom it finally dissolves— that Self is devoid of karma and the like, and is self-luminous.
I am Śiva, I am Śiva, I am Śiva, I am Śiva. || 37 ||
He upon whose crown is the moon, on whose forehead is fire, on whose arm is the king of serpents, on whose neck is blackness,
and on whose body is a beloved woman— may that god, who is equal to him [Śiva], protect you.
I do not know, I do not know, I do not know, I do not know. || 38 ||
Those people who, having attained supreme devotion, worship the Lord of Ambikā with reverence by means of this hymn,
they shall be fearless at the time of death; such people worship Him.
The Lord, ever seated in the center of the heart-lotus. || 39 ||
O Śambhu, this *Bhujaṅgapriyā-kalpa* has been composed by me in the *Bhujaṅgaprayāta* meter. A person who recites this hymn with great devotion—
One attains excellent sons, long life, health, and sovereignty. || 40 ||
The Śivabhujaṅga is complete.
